title: Mixed-language doctor-patient consultation -> English clinical note
business_question: A clinic records an outpatient consultation held in Hinglish / Malayalam-English / Tamil-English / Bengali-English / Marathi-English. Which model turns it into a correct structured English note, and which one invents medicines or doses (the safety risk)?

dataset.name: uc05 synthetic OPD consultations
dataset.how_made: 40 fictional outpatient dialogues (8 per language pair; fever, diabetes, hypertension, pregnancy follow-up, paediatrics; 11-16 turns) written by an LLM author (Claude) with gold facts (complaint, duration, vitals, diagnosis, each medicine with dose/frequency/duration, allergies, red flags, follow-up). Every dialogue has a trap: a drug mentioned but not prescribed, a dose corrected mid-conversation, or a late-disclosed allergy. 15 dialogues voiced with gemini-3.8-flash-tts (2 prebuilt voices). Fake names only.

findings: From the dialogue text, every cloud model wrote a usable English note. fact_recall_overall over 40 dialogues: gemini-3.8-flash 1.00, gemini-pro-latest 1.00, claude-sonnet-5.5 1.00, gemini-3.8-flash with thinking, gpt-5.4-mini with thinking, claude-haiku-5.5 with thinking and gpt-5.5 all 0.99, sarvam-105b with thinking 0.98, gpt-5.4-mini 0.97, sarvam-105b 0.96 (CI 0.94-0.98), claude-haiku-5.5 without thinking 0.93.

Safety metric: no text-track system listed a drug that was not prescribed or a dose that was never said (hallucinated meds/doses per note = 0.00 for all, n=30-40). All 40 traps were handled: refused antibiotics, stopped drugs, self-medication, mid-sentence dose corrections and late-disclosed allergies. With an explicit 'final prescription only' instruction, these models do not invent medicines.

The errors that remain are frequency errors, and they are clinically meaningful. 'Paracetamol 5 ml only when fever is above 100, not more than 4 times a day' (an as-needed/SOS dose with a daily cap) was written as scheduled QID or TDS by sarvam-105b (d03, d13), sarvam-105b with thinking (d03, d19, d27, d28), claude-haiku-5.5 (d03, d13, d19, d27, d28), gpt-5.4-mini (d27) and the gpt-4o-transcribe pipeline. sarvam-105b also turned two 'morning one, night one' (BD) prescriptions into OD (d28 cefixime, d31 calcium). Medication exactness (drug + dose + frequency): gemini-3.8-flash 1.00, claude-haiku-5.5 with thinking 1.00, all frontier models 1.00, gpt-5.4-mini 0.99, sarvam-105b 0.93, sarvam-105b with thinking 0.91, claude-haiku-5.5 without thinking 0.90.

Writing the note in English is not automatic. Share of notes with no Indic-script text: sarvam-105b, gemini (all modes), the frontier models and all audio pipelines 1.00, gpt-5.4-mini 0.95, claude-haiku-5.5 0.60 (0.90 with thinking), qwen3-30b-local 0.68, sarvam-30b-local 0.58. Claude Haiku and the local models often copied the patient's words in Hindi, Tamil or Bengali into the complaint or red-flag fields, e.g. 'बुखार, पूरे बदन में दर्द…' as the chief complaint.

Self-hosted models (Q4_K_M, thinking off, all 40 dialogues), fact recall / medication exactness: qwen3-30b-local 0.79 / 0.87 with 0 invented medicines; sarvam-30b-local 0.78 / 0.79 with one invented medicine (d25: it listed 'Dolo 650' as a second drug next to paracetamol, which could lead to a double paracetamol dose). Neither listed a trap drug as prescribed. Most of their recall loss is complaint and red-flag text left in the source language; vitals recall stays at 0.95-0.97. p50 is 12 s per note on the shared Mac.

Thinking did not help sarvam-105b here: medication exactness 0.91 with thinking vs 0.93 without. It cost 173k reasoning tokens for 40 notes, latency rose from 1.8 s to 25.8 s (p50), one note was not valid JSON (d37), and one omitted metformin after a mid-sentence dose correction (d18). For claude-haiku-5.5 and gpt-5.4-mini, thinking did help (0.90 to 1.00, and 0.97 to 0.99 fact recall).

Audio track, scored on the same 15 voiced dialogues (fact recall / medication exactness): gemini-3.8-flash directly on the audio 1.00 / 1.00, the same as its text-track score. gpt-4o-transcribe + gpt-5.4-mini 0.98 / 0.90. saaras:v3 translate with diarization + sarvam-105b 0.94 / 0.87, vitals 0.88, red flags 0.74. The note-writer is not the problem: sarvam-105b scores 0.97 / 0.97 on the gold text of those same 15 dialogues, so the STT step costs the Sarvam pipeline about 3 points of fact recall and 10 of medication exactness.

saaras:v3 translate-mode errors we saw: (1) d10 Malayalam: the sentence prescribing telmisartan 40 mg was dropped from the transcript entirely ('Both should be eaten regularly' survives, without the drug), so the note lists only amlodipine; this is an omission, not an invented drug. (2) Spoken numbers: Marathi 'one hundred point eight' became 'one hundred and eight' (temperature 108 °F, d35); Tamil 'BP 124 by 80' became 'BP 125' (d17); Marathi 'BP 116 by 74' became '116 divided by 74. What is this reverse multiplication?' (d33). (3) Drug spelling: 'Glimipride' for glimepiride (d26). Diarization was right at the coarse level: 2 speakers in 15/15 files, and the median ratio of detected to scripted speaker changes was 1.0.

saaras:v4 (released 25 Sep 2026) on the same 15 dialogues, same diarized batch API, note by sarvam-105b. Fact recall / medication exactness / red-flag recall: v3 translate 0.94 / 0.87 / 0.74; v4 translate 0.93 / 0.83 / 0.86; v4 codemix (source-language transcript with English terms kept, then sarvam-105b translates) 0.97 / 0.83 / 0.93. v4 fixes the spoken-decimal error: Marathi 'one hundred point eight' now comes out as 100.8, not 108 (d35). It does not fix the dropped prescription: in d10 all three saaras variants omit the sentence 'with it, Telmisartan 40 mg once a day at night' that comes right after the diagnosis sentence, while gpt-4o-transcribe has it word for word, so the sentence is in the audio. v4 translate added new errors: it lost a dose correction (d02 glimepiride 2 mg instead of the corrected 1 mg), garbled glimepiride as 'Gimi Pride', which is scored as an unsupported medicine (0.07 per note), and read 'BP 124 by 80' as 'BP 120' (d17). v4 codemix had no unsupported medicines and is the best Sarvam audio pipeline here, though medication exactness (0.83) is still below gpt-4o-transcribe + gpt-5.4-mini (0.90) and Gemini direct (1.00). The 95% CIs overlap heavily with n=15. Diarization: 2 speakers detected in 15/15 files for both v4 modes. The model name 'saaras:v4-multispk' is rejected with HTTP 400 'deprecated, use saaras-multispeaker'; plain 'saaras:v4' accepts with_diarization=true and returns diarized_transcript. Batch jobs still took about 10 s, and outputs are still named by upload index.

saaras:v3 batch quirk: output files are named by upload index ('0.json', '1.json', ...), not after the input file. Two jobs downloaded into one folder overwrite each other, so map outputs via job_details[i].inputs/outputs from the status endpoint. Our first run lost 12 of 15 transcripts this way. Batch jobs of 3 files (about 70 s of audio each) finished in 10-11 s.

gemini-3.8-flash-tts multi-speaker requires each text part to carry speech_metadata.speaker. A single prompt with 'Doctor: … Patient: …' lines is rejected with HTTP 400. 15 dialogues produced 1,081 s of audio. Every gold dose number appears in at least one of the two STT transcripts, so the TTS did not drop doses.

Separately, asking gemini-3.8-flash for a verbatim transcript of d01 left out the first three turns, although the audio contains them (a clip of the first 15 s transcribes fine). Its notes from audio were still complete, so this affects plain transcription only.

Speed per note, p50/p95: gpt-5.4-mini 1.5/1.9 s, sarvam-105b 1.8/2.2 s, claude-haiku-5.5 2.5/3.4 s, gemini-3.8-flash 4.4/13.3 s, gemini-3.8-flash with thinking 13.8/23.1 s, sarvam-105b with thinking 25.8/45.5 s. Audio: saaras batch (about 10 s per job) then sarvam-105b at 2.2 s; Gemini audio-to-note in one call at 5.7 s.
caveats: The 40 dialogues and gold facts are synthetic, written by an LLM author (Claude). They are clean and well-structured compared with real OPD talk: no crosstalk, no background noise, every vital stated clearly. The task is near the ceiling for strong models.

The audio is TTS (2 studio voices, no noise, no overlap), so the STT and audio results are optimistic compared with a real clinic recording. Recorded consultations with consent would be the next step.

Free-text fields (complaint, diagnosis, red flags, follow-up) are scored by alias word overlap with a small synonym map. Correct paraphrases can still be marked as misses, so absolute red-flag recall is understated. All systems are scored with the same matcher, and we audited the misses by hand.

The 'hallucinated dose' check only catches dose numbers that never appear in the dialogue. A real but wrong dose taken from elsewhere in the conversation shows up as a medication-exactness error instead.

Frontier models ran on 30 of 40 dialogues (evenly spread across languages; dataset.frontier_subset_ids). Local models ran all 40 text dialogues. Use values_frontier_subset / values_audio_subset to compare like with like.
n is small (40 notes, 15 audio, 13 dialogues with allergies), so CIs are wide. sarvam-105b's medication exactness CI is 0.85-0.99.
verdict: For an AI scribe working from a transcript, gemini-3.8-flash (thinking off) is the pick in the price-matched tier: perfect on every field we scored, no invented drugs, 4 s per note. gpt-5.4-mini (1.5 s) is a close, faster second. sarvam-105b is as safe (it never invented a medicine) and fast (1.8 s), but it gets about 1 in 15 frequencies wrong, typically turning an as-needed dose into a scheduled one. Reasoning mode does not fix that and makes it 14x slower, so any Sarvam-based scribe needs a frequency check by the doctor. From audio, sending the recording straight to gemini-3.8-flash was the most accurate path in our test (100% on 15 dialogues). The Sarvam pipeline is cheap (₹45/hour of audio with diarization) and diarizes correctly. Use saaras:v4 in codemix mode, then sarvam-105b: on 15 dialogues it scored 0.97 fact recall vs 0.94 for v3 translate, and it fixes v3's spoken-number errors. But every saaras version dropped the same prescription sentence in one Malayalam consultation, and medication exactness stays at 0.83 vs 1.00 for Gemini on the raw audio, so always show the doctor the transcript next to the note. Self-hosted 30B models are not ready to be an unsupervised scribe: about 1 in 5 medicine lines have an error, and 30-40% of notes are not fully in English. qwen3-30b-local was the safer of the two.

examples.trap: Mother gave leftover Azithral; doctor stops it.
examples.dialogue:
Doctor: नमस्ते, आइए। बच्चे का नाम क्या है और उम्र?
Attendant: आरव है, चार साल का। दो दिन से खांसी-ज़ुकाम है और बुखार भी है।
Doctor: बुखार कितना है? रात को साँस लेने में कोई दिक्कत?
Attendant: रात को 101 तक गया था। साँस ठीक है, बस नाक बंद रहती है।
Doctor: अभी temperature 100.6 है, oxygen यानी SpO2 98 percent है, बढ़िया है। वज़न 16 kilo है।
Attendant: डॉक्टर, घर में बड़े बेटे की Azithral की बोतल पड़ी थी, कल रात एक खुराक दे दी थी।
Doctor: नहीं, वो बंद कर दीजिए। ये viral infection है, upper respiratory tract infection, इसमें antibiotic की ज़रूरत नहीं है। बिना पूछे antibiotic मत दीजिए।
Attendant: जी ठीक है। इसे किसी दवा से allergy नहीं है।
Doctor: अच्छा। बुखार के लिए Paracetamol syrup, Calpol 250, 5 ml, जब बुखार सौ से ऊपर हो तभी, दिन में चार बार से ज़्यादा नहीं, तीन दिन तक।
Doctor: ज़ुकाम के लिए Cetirizine syrup 2.5 ml, रात को सोने से पहले, पाँच दिन।
Attendant: खाना कम खा रहा है, क्या करूँ?
Doctor: थोड़ा-थोड़ा करके पानी और दाल का पानी देते रहिए। अगर साँस तेज़ चले, पसली चले, बच्चा पानी पीना बंद कर दे या दौरा पड़े, तो तुरंत emergency में लाइए।
Attendant: जी समझ गई। फिर कब आएँ?
Doctor: तीन दिन बाद दिखाइए, अगर बुखार तब भी रहे।

examples.trap: Atenolol stopped because of low pulse; weight said in Malayalam words.
examples.dialogue:
Doctor: ലീലാമ്മേ, വരൂ. എന്തുണ്ട് വിശേഷം?
Patient: ഡോക്ടറേ, പത്തു ദിവസമായി രാവിലെ എഴുന്നേൽക്കുമ്പോൾ തലവേദനയാണ്. ചിലപ്പോൾ നെഞ്ചിടിപ്പ് പതുക്കെയാണെന്ന് തോന്നും.
Doctor: ഇപ്പോൾ ഏതൊക്കെ ഗുളികയാണ് കഴിക്കുന്നത്?
Patient: Amlodipine 5 mg രാവിലെ ഒന്ന്. പിന്നെ Atenolol 50 mg രാത്രി.
Doctor: നോക്കട്ടെ. BP 158 by 94 ആണ്. Pulse 56 മാത്രമേ ഉള്ളൂ, അത് കുറവാണ്. Weight അറുപത്തിയാറ് കിലോ.
Patient: അതു പ്രശ്നമാണോ ഡോക്ടറേ?
Doctor: Pulse കുറയാൻ കാരണം Atenolol ആവാം. അതുകൊണ്ട് Atenolol ഇന്നു മുതൽ നിർത്തണം. ഏതെങ്കിലും മരുന്നിനോട് അലർജി ഉണ്ടോ?
Patient: ഇല്ല ഡോക്ടറേ, ഒന്നിനോടും ഇല്ല.
Doctor: ശരി. BP ഇപ്പോഴും control-ൽ അല്ല, ഇത് uncontrolled hypertension ആണ്. Amlodipine 5 mg രാവിലെ ഒരു നേരം തുടരുക. കൂടെ Telmisartan 40 mg, ദിവസം ഒരു നേരം, രാത്രി. രണ്ടും സ്ഥിരമായി കഴിക്കണം.
Patient: ഉപ്പ് കുറയ്ക്കണോ?
Doctor: തീർച്ചയായും. അച്ചാറും പപ്പടവും കുറയ്ക്കണം. നെഞ്ചുവേദന വന്നാലോ, ഒരു വശം തളർന്നാലോ, സംസാരം കുഴഞ്ഞാലോ, തലകറങ്ങി വീണാലോ ഉടനെ ആശുപത്രിയിൽ വരണം.
Patient: ശരി. അടുത്തത് എപ്പോഴാണ്?
Doctor: രണ്ടാഴ്ച കഴിഞ്ഞ് വരൂ. വീട്ടിൽ BP നോക്കി എഴുതി കൊണ്ടുവരണം.

Patient: হ্যাঁ, মায়ের ছিল। আর কোনো ওষুধে আমার allergy নেই।
Doctor: আপনার type 2 diabetes হয়েছে। Metformin 500 mg দিচ্ছি, সকাল-রাত... না দাঁড়ান, sugar যেহেতু বেশি, metformin 1000 mg করেই দিই, সকালে আর রাতে খাবারের পরে একটা করে। এটা regular চলবে।
Patient: শুধু এটাই?
Doctor: আর glimepiride 1 mg, সকালে breakfast-এর আগে একটা, এটাও continue করবেন।
Patient: ওষুধ খেয়ে কোনো সমস্যা হলে?
Doctor: যদি হঠাৎ মাথা ঘোরে, খুব ঘাম হয়, হাত-পা কাঁপে, তাহলে বুঝবেন sugar কমে গেছে, সঙ্গে সঙ্গে চিনি খাবেন আর আমাকে জানাবেন। আর পায়ে কোনো ঘা হলে ফেলে রাখবেন না।

Doctor: 1 মাস পরে আসবেন, HbA1c আর fasting sugar test করিয়ে।
Patient: ঠিক আছে ডাক্তারবাবু।

examples.trap: Amoxicillin dose corrected from 5 ml to 7.5 ml after weighing; temperature spoken in words.
examples.dialogue:
Attendant: डॉक्टर, माझ्या मुलीचा कान 2 दिवसांपासून दुखतोय, रात्रभर रडत होती. ती 6 वर्षांची आहे.
Doctor: ताप आहे का?
Attendant: हो, थोडा ताप आहे.
Doctor: Temperature शंभर पूर्णांक आठ आहे. कान बघतो... कानाचा पडदा लाल झालाय. हे acute otitis media आहे, म्हणजे कानाचं infection.
Attendant: तिला कोणत्याही औषधाची allergy नाही.
Doctor: Amoxicillin syrup देतो, 5 ml दिवसातून तीन वेळा... थांबा, तिचं weight किती आहे?
Attendant: आत्ताच मोजलं, 20 kg.
Doctor: मग 20 kg साठी 5 ml कमी पडेल. Amoxicillin syrup 7.5 ml, दिवसातून तीन वेळा, 7 दिवस पूर्ण द्या.
Doctor: आणि ताप आला किंवा कान दुखला तरच paracetamol syrup 6 ml द्या.
Attendant: अजून काही काळजी?
Doctor: कानातून पू आला, ताप उतरत नसेल, किंवा मान ताठ झाली तर लगेच घेऊन या.
Attendant: पुन्हा कधी दाखवायचं?
Doctor: 5 दिवसांनी परत दाखवा.
